paper.title: Family Visitation Patterns during Incarceration in Denmark
paper.code_data_availability: No code or data availability statement. The data 'were routinely collected by the Danish Prison and Probation Services for administrative purposes and were made accessible for research in a de-identified version by Statistics Denmark …

registers.name_in_paper: administrative data on all incarcerations and visits (Danish Prison and Probation Services)
registers.role: sample frame; outcomes (visits); treatment/predictors (sentence, facility, transfers, pre-trial)
variables_mentioned: time, place and duration of the visit
entry and release/transfer dates for all correctional facilities

registers.name_in_paper: data on all registered convictions (supplied by The Danish National Police)
registers.years: Penal Act convictions since 1980; Special Acts violations since 1992
variables_mentioned: number of previous convictions for Penal Act violations since 1980
number of previous convictions for Special Acts violations since 1992

registers.name_in_paper: administrative registers made accessible by Statistics Denmark (on prior criminal justice contact, socioeconomic status, and demographic characteristics including family structure)
registers.role: predictors (demographics, family structure, employment, income, education)
variables_mentioned: family structure registered on January 1st the year of incarceration
whether the inmate is a parent
employment status measured November 1st the year prior to incarceration
gross income the year prior to incarceration (10,000s DKK, 2015 level)

registers.name_in_paper: geocoded data on prisons/jails and inmates' residence
registers.role: predictors (driving distance between facility and home)
variables_mentioned: shortest driving distance in hours of traveling time

linkages: Unique de-identified ID numbers combined with unique case numbers to track incarcerated individuals and their visits across all facilities, new sentences and visits
Unique ID numbers used to link the incarceration data to administrative registers made accessible by Statistics Denmark
Incarceration data linked to data on all registered convictions supplied by The Danish National Police
Facility addresses and inmates' residential addresses linked through geocoding to compute driving distance

sample.universe: All incarcerations and visits in facilities under the Danish Prison and Probation Services, 2004-2014
sample.unit_of_observation: Incarceration spell (5,411 spells covering 5,039 individual inmates); visitation measured monthly over the first 12 months of the spell
selection_rules: Incarceration spells that start between 2004 and 2013
Spells that take place in prisons or jails; spells in halfway houses and deportation centers excluded
Spells that last at least one year
For the regressions predicting class membership, the sample is further restricted to spells assigned to the outcome class or to the reference class 3

construction_notes: Only visits by family members are counted; family members constitute approximately 75% of all visitors (the rest are friends and professionals or volunteers).
Visitation is measured as the monthly number of visits and the average duration of visits per month for each of the first 12 months (24 variables entering the latent class model).
Facility type is the type of facility in which the inmate spends the most time during the first year: jails, closed prisons (reference), open prisons, psychiatric institutions.
Distance is the shortest driving distance between the modal facility and the inmate's residence, in hours of traveling time; for public-transport users this understates actual travel time.
In approximately 30% of cases the distance could not be calculated because of missing or ungeocodable addresses; these are coded with a missing-distance dummy.
Sentence length is grouped into less than two years (reference), two-three years, three-five years, and five years and above.
Crime type categories: homicide, sex crimes, violence (reference), robbery, drug crimes, property crime, vandalism, other penal offences, traffic offences, Special Acts and other violations.
Prior convictions: number of previous prison sentences; Penal Act convictions counted since 1980; Special Acts violations counted since 1992 (when registration of traffic fines changed).
Family structure is registered on January 1st of the year of incarceration (lives alone = reference, with partner/spouse, with parents) and parenthood separately.
Employment status is measured November 1st of the year prior to incarceration (employed = reference; in education; unemployed/outside labor force/missing).
Gross income is measured the year prior to incarceration in 10,000s DKK at the 2015 level.
Education: primary or missing education (reference), upper secondary, tertiary.
All regressors in the Figure 2 models are standardized to mean 0 and standard deviation 1; year and month dummies are also included.
The abstract states N = 5,441 while the Data section and Table 1 state 5,411 incarceration spells; 5,411 is used here.

claims.statement: Drugs (crime type) is associated with a lower probability of belonging to latent visitation class 1 (low, stable levels of family visitation) rather than to class 3 (medium, declining) during the first year of incarceration.

register_source.value: Danish Prison and Probation Services incarceration data (no Statistics Denmark register code given)

definition.value: Indicator for being incarcerated for a drug crime; crime type comes from the incarceration data and is coded as homicide, sex crimes, violence (reference category), robbery, drug crimes, property crime, vandalism, other penal offences, traffic offences, and Special Acts and other violations. Standardized to mean 0 and standard deviation 1 before estimation (Figure 2 note).

timing.value: Offence of the current incarceration spell

outcome.label: Membership in latent family visitation class 1 versus class 3 (medium, declining)

register_source.value: Danish Prison and Probation Services visitation data (no Statistics Denmark register code given); latent class constructed by the authors

definition.value: 0/1 indicator for being assigned to Class 1 (low, stable), characterized by low, stable levels of family visitation, rather than to the reference class 3 (medium level of family visitation, which declined over time), from a five-class latent profile model fitted to the monthly number of family visits and the average duration of family visits in each of the first 12 months of incarceration (24 variables). Only family visitors are counted.

timing.value: Class membership summarises visitation over months 1-12 of the incarceration spell

units.value: change in the probability of belonging to the class rather than to class 3 (outcome on a 0/1 scale) per one standard deviation of the standardized predictor

estimand.target_population: Incarceration spells in Danish prisons and jails that started 2004-2013 and lasted at least one year, whose first-year visitation pattern was assigned either to Class 1 (low, stable) or to the reference class 3
estimand.time_horizon: Latent class membership is defined over months 1-12 of the incarceration spell; the predictors are measured before, at the start of, or during that first year

population.description: Incarceration spells in Danish prisons or jails starting 2004-2013 and lasting at least one year (5,411 spells covering 5,039 individual inmates); this regression uses the 4,150 spells assigned to Class 1 (low, stable) or to class 3
population.period: Incarceration spells starting 2004-2013, observed over their first year; visitation data cover 2004-2014
population.selection: Incarceration spells that (a) start between 2004 and 2013, (b) take place in prisons or jails (halfway houses and deportation centers excluded), and (c) last at least one year; the regression sample is further restricted to spells assigned to the outcome class or to the reference class 3

identification.source_of_variation: No exogenous variation is used. Cross-sectional variation across incarceration spells in offence, sentence, facility, criminal history, demographic and socioeconomic characteristics is used to predict which latent visitation class a spell falls into, with class 3 as the reference.

key_assumptions.assumption: Latent class membership estimated from the five-class latent profile model is treated as an observed outcome in the regressions; classification uncertainty is not carried into the second stage.
Local independence: conditional on the latent class, the 24 monthly visitation indicators (number and average duration of visits in each of the first 12 months) are independent of one another.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated as the defining property of the latent class model in the Methods section; no test reported.

lhs: monthly number of family visits, months 1-12
rhs: average monthly duration of family visits, months 1-12

average monthly duration of family visits, months 1-12

key_assumptions.assumption: The conditional probability of belonging to the outcome class rather than to class 3 is linear in the standardized covariates (linear probability model).

The analytic sample is conditioned on the incarceration spell starting 2004-2013, taking place in a prison or jail, and lasting at least one year; the authors state this selection limits generalizability.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The sample restriction and its cost in generalizability are stated in the Data section and revisited in the Discussion.

implies_edges.from: incarceration spell lasts at least one year
implies_edges.to: inclusion in the analytic sample

key_assumptions.assumption: Driving distance that could not be computed (about 30% of cases) is handled with a missing-distance dummy rather than imputation, so the distance coefficient is identified off the geocodable cases.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The missing-distance dummy and the 30% figure are stated in the Data section.

key_assumptions.assumption: The coefficients are read as conditional associations (predictors of class membership), not as causal effects; no exogenous variation is invoked.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper speaks throughout of predicting class membership and of factors being 'associated with' patterns.

threats_discussed: The analytical sample is restricted to spells of at least one year, which the authors say comes at the cost of generalizability
The sample holds much larger shares of sexual offences, homicide, robbery and drug offences than the general population of inmates
Driving distance could not be calculated in about 30% of cases because of missing or ungeocodable addresses
The driving-time distance measure understates actual travel time for visitors relying on public transportation
Results are from a Danish setting with a low incarceration rate and a more generous welfare state than the U.S. context the literature comes from

ambiguities: Visible in the class 1 panel of Figure 2 but not discussed in the text, which says crime type 'did not appear to matter much'.

evidence.annotation: Note. N=4,150 (class 1 vs. 3), N=1,773 (class 2 vs. 3), N=1,435 (class 4 vs. 3), N=1,611 (class 5 vs. 3). Coefficients that do not reach statistical significance (p < 0.05) are not shown. See Table A-2 in the Online Supporting Material for all coefficients. Variables are standardized with a mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1. Also included are year and month dummies. Reference categories are as follows: crime type—violence; facility—mostly closed prison; sentence length—<2 years; employment status—employed; education—primary/missing education.

evidence.how: Sign read off the Class 1 (low, stable) panel of Figure 2: the plotted marker and the whole of its confidence interval lie on one side of the zero line.

evidence.annotation: Note. Figures show the mean number of visits and duration of visits for each month conditional on latent class membership. The proportion assigned to each class are as follows: class 1—54.8%; class 2—10.8%; class 3—21.9%; class 4—4.6%; class 5—7.9%.

evidence.how: The share of incarceration spells assigned to class 1, printed as 54.8% in the Figure 1 note, divided by 100 to put it on the 0/1 scale of the class-membership outcome. It is the share in the full sample of 5,411 spells, not in the class-1-versus-class-3 estimation subsample.

The latent class is both the treatment here and the object constructed from the outcome variables, so the relationship is definitional rather than causal; it is recorded because the abstract states the heterogeneity finding.

evidence.annotation: Note. Figures show the mean number of visits and duration of visits for each month conditional on latent class membership. The proportion assigned to each class are as follows: class 1—54.8%; class 2—10.8%; class 3—21.9%; class 4—4.6%; class 5—7.9%.

value.claimed_domain: Inmates serving comparatively long (at least one year) sentences in Denmark; the authors caution that the select sample and the Danish context limit transferability
boundary_conditions: Based on a select sample of inmates in Denmark
Inmates received comparatively long sentences from the Danish perspective
